title: Morning
intro: Morning makes being seen the cause of disappearing. The speaker tries to produce a flawless self, draws the camera's attention and discovers that the light is melting a body made of snow. Even relief is visible but unreachable. Once the self has dissolved into an anonymous historical current, an ordinary phone call asks who he wants to become today. The question could offer reinvention, but after the preceding loss it also sounds like another demand to supply a presentable identity before the day can begin.
reading: Visibility destroys the identity it promises to recognise; daily reinvention is an opportunity under pressure.

revisions.editorial-50-headlong: The method is collision while the desired result is flawlessness. He tries every available move and angle, but constant activity does not establish control. The opening memory of punishment for disobedience puts additional pressure behind the pursuit: getting the self right already has consequences attached. That combination prepares the later public image as something worked at intensely, rather than a effortless expression of confidence.
revisions.editorial-50-quiet-visible: Quiet loneliness comes directly before being watched by everyone. The two conditions coexist. Attention supplies exposure without necessarily supplying somebody who can respond when help is needed; the unreachable ice bucket makes that failure concrete. The song's problem is therefore not solved by simply becoming more visible. Visibility is already abundant, and soon becomes the threatening force itself.
revisions.t50-n2: The delayed discovery that he is a snowman reorganises the earlier scene. The camera's flattering brightness, sunlight and inaccessible ice now belong to one threat. What would help an ordinary performer be recognised destroys the form of this performer. The metaphor is unusually exact: attention and erasure are not opposite stages of a career here, but linked effects of the same exposure.
revisions.t50-phrase-become-today: The caller asks who he wants to become, rather than what he plans to do. After the melting sequence, identity itself appears as something required anew for the day's activity. The question leaves room for possibility, but its repetition also makes that possibility sound compulsory. No new self is chosen in the lyric. The song ends with the request still ringing, not with a completed rebirth.
